body: Hmm, after updating the script with some fixes, I'm not sure that I can recreate this behavior.
Okay, I've looked into it further, and it appears that the error is triggered when a secondary index is used to successfully look up a recently-inserted row.

@kmuthukk @mbautin From what I can tell, truncating the table makes the issue more likely to occur:

```
$ ./error_poc.amd64 2 172.161.59.54
2019/07/25 20:27:32 workers_per_hostname: 2
2019/07/25 20:27:32 hosts: [172.161.59.54]
2019/07/25 20:27:32 0 inserts, 0 selects
2019/07/25 20:27:32 established connection 1/2
2019/07/25 20:27:32 established connection 2/2
2019/07/25 20:27:33 34 inserts, 35 selects
2019/07/25 20:27:34 275 inserts, 272 selects
2019/07/25 20:27:35 507 inserts, 528 selects
2019/07/25 20:27:36 747 inserts, 731 selects
2019/07/25 20:27:37 983 inserts, 952 selects
2019/07/25 20:27:38 1218 inserts, 1176 selects
^C
$ echo "TRUNCATE TABLE t;" | psql -h 172.161.59.54 -U postgres -p 5433 -d error_poc
TRUNCATE TABLE
$ ./error_poc.amd64 2 172.161.59.54
2019/07/25 20:27:46 workers_per_hostname: 2
2019/07/25 20:27:46 hosts: [172.161.59.54]
2019/07/25 20:27:46 0 inserts, 0 selects
2019/07/25 20:27:47 established connection 1/2
2019/07/25 20:27:47 established connection 2/2
2019/07/25 20:27:47 failed to select: pq: Query error: Restart read required at: { read: { physical: 1564086467290516 logical: 2 } local_limit: { physical: 1564086467299331 } global_limit: <min> in_txn_limit: <max> serial_no: 0 }
```

@mbautin @rkarthik007 This is happening for me after `DROP`ing a database, not just `TRUNCATE`ing:

```
$ echo "DROP DATABASE error_poc; CREATE DATABASE error_poc;" | psql -h 172.161.59.54 -U postgres -p 5433
DROP DATABASE
CREATE DATABASE
$ echo "CREATE TABLE t (a VARCHAR PRIMARY KEY, b VARCHAR); CREATE INDEX ON t (b, a);" | psql -h 172.161.59.54 -U postgres -p 5433 -d error_poc
CREATE TABLE
CREATE INDEX
$ ./error_poc.amd64 2 172.161.59.54
2019/07/29 05:10:51 workers_per_hostname: 2
2019/07/29 05:10:51 hosts: [172.161.59.54]
2019/07/29 05:10:51 0 inserts, 0 selects
2019/07/29 05:10:52 0 inserts, 0 selects
2019/07/29 05:10:53 0 inserts, 0 selects
2019/07/29 05:10:54 0 inserts, 0 selects
2019/07/29 05:10:55 established connection 1/2
2019/07/29 05:10:55 established connection 2/2
2019/07/29 05:10:55 failed to select: pq: Query error: Restart read required at: { read: { physical: 1564377055355903 logical: 1 } local_limit: { physical: 1564377055373279 } global_limit: <min> in_txn_limit: <max> serial_no: 0 }
```

This matches what I see in my own benchmark code, which quickly gives an equivalent error in an equivalent situation:

```
2019/07/29 05:05:01 client log: 2019/07/29 05:05:01 error during SELECT query: pq: Query error: Restart read required at: { read: { physical: 156437670109145
9 } local_limit: { physical: 1564376701131261 } global_limit: <min> in_txn_limit: <max> serial_no: 0 }
```

@rw - thanks for pointing this out! This is going to cause some failed operations (but should not cause any errors).

@mbautin @spolitov @ttyusupov - could you please take a look at why we get read restarts in Robert's case?
